name: Soil Moisture
description: Path 2 (grass path) is highly susceptible to travel time changes based on soil moisture. Wet soil increases resistance and slippage, drastically increasing travel time. This is likely the *primary* driver of multimodality; dry conditions allow for fast travel, while wet conditions cause significantly slower travel. We'd expect distinct time groups based on recent rainfall/irrigation.

name: Rainfall
description: Directly impacts soil moisture. Even a small amount of rain can significantly affect Path 2's traversability, leading to distinct travel time clusters. Rainfall events are discrete and impactful.

name: Time of Day
description: Affects both paths. Dew formation on grass (Path 2) increases moisture. Solar heating can bake and harden Path 1, or soften/compact Path 2. Time of day also influences lighting conditions for camera-based navigation, potentially slowing down Path 1 or introducing errors.

name: Crop Row Condition (Path 2)
description: Variations in crop row height, density, and presence of fallen leaves/debris on Path 2 will influence travel time. Uneven ground or obstructions will cause slowdowns and could create distinct time groups.

name: Sunlight Intensity
description: Affects camera performance on Path 1 and contributes to soil moisture evaporation. High glare can impact computer vision algorithms used for Path 1 navigation, while direct sunlight dries Path 2, altering its traversability.

name: Robot Load
description: The weight of any tools/collected samples significantly impacts slippage on Path 2 and power consumption on both paths. Different loads will yield different travel times and potentially create clusters.

name: Path 1 Surface Condition
description: The composition and condition of the track (Path 1) - e.g., gravel, dirt, compaction. Potholes, ruts or loose gravel increase travel time and introduce variability.

name: Plant Growth Stage
description: As crops grow, they obstruct Path 2, increasing travel time. Different growth stages lead to different levels of obstruction and therefore distinct travel time profiles.

name: Wind Speed
description: High winds can increase resistance, especially for the robot, affecting both paths. On Path 2, wind can also blow debris into the path, creating obstacles.

name: Robot Battery Level
description: As the battery discharges, motor performance may decrease, potentially impacting travel speed on both paths. A lower battery may cause the robot to reduce speed or struggle on uneven terrain.

name: Weather Events (recent)
description: Recent severe weather (storms, hail) can significantly affect both paths – creating debris, flooding, or damaging the track. This creates abrupt shifts in travel time.

name: Crop Type
description: Different crops have different row spacings and growth habits, impacting the space and surface conditions on Path 2.  This will affect robot maneuverability and speed.

name: Task Type
description: If the robot is performing different tasks (e.g. spraying vs. inspection), the tools used could change the load, and the operation itself may affect the path taken and speed.

name: Slope of Paths
description: If either path has significant slopes, these will affect travel time. Variations in slope *along* the path will also add variability.

name: Obstacle Density on Path 1
description: While the outer edge is supposed to be clear, debris or unexpected obstacles (small rocks, fallen branches) could occasionally appear on Path 1 causing delays.  Less likely to be the primary driver, but can contribute.
